system.summary: One-part word code of number pairs from an unidentified printed list, with words spelled letter by letter as line-letter pairs on the title page of the 1778 Army List.
system.sibling_key: The spelling part is the Haldimand-Clinton Army List line-letter cipher of 1778-1781 (Haldimand's key sheet, B.147 pp. 402-405), used here unchanged.
system.notes: Spelled words are marked x or underlined, the first coordinate often dittoed; a letter has several pairs where it recurs on the page, hence homophones. 174 distinct word codes seen in the three letters, first number 1-58, second 1-34; a few carry written suffixes (communicat+ed, Vermont+eers, who+se).

prior_solution.where: Clear texts kept with the ciphers at Quebec: Clinton's own clear quadruplicate (B.148 pp. 8-9), and the Carleton letters in Haldimand's register B.146 pp. 50, 54 and B.148 p. 102. Clinton's letter of 22 Feb is printed in full (clear text) in Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections vol. 20 (1892) pp. 2-4, found 13 Nov 2026 after the work. The Carleton letters: English summaries in Brymner's calendars (Report on Canadian Archives 1885, 1887) and headings in the HMC Royal Institution calendar vol. III (1907); not found in Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections vols. 9-11, 19-20. No modern reading found.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the research direction and the posting restraint; AI agents located the sources, transcribed, aligned, froze and ran the held-out test, and packaged the folder. Our own AI coordinator checked the freeze hashes before the clear copy was opened; the order of events rests on our agents' own file times. A second AI agent of ours later rechecked the work without being shown our conclusions. No human reading verification recorded.
tools: frozen held-out prediction and scorer (preclear/, postclear/score.py)
models: Codex (GPT-6) agents and coordinator, 12 Nov 2026 research packages (by the package records)
Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), 13 Nov 2026 packaging, strict measure and validation

solution.what: Haldimand's key sheet (B.147 pp. 402-405) matched to the title page of the 1778 Army List: 151 of 155 worked examples, 232 of 249 letters of his 16 Dec 1778 letter.
Carleton 6 Sep 1782 cipher (B.148 pp. 93-94) transcribed before the clear copy was read beyond its opening lines.

6 Sep aligned word for word with the clear text in B.146 p. 50: 94 word codes (66 distinct), 15 spelled words, 95 of 96 letters on the Army List key; a mod-29 reading of all pairs had failed because it mixed word codes with spelled pairs.

Clinton 22 Feb cipher (B.148 pp. 11-11B) transcribed in full and aligned with the clear quadruplicate: 100 distinct word codes (26 shared with 6 Sep), 39 of 44 spelled words exact on the unchanged key, 5 kept as mismatches.

Freeze at 23:44 UTC: the Clinton code table, the key and a full transcription of the 25 Sep cipher with its mechanical predictions; hashes checked by our own AI coordinator before the clear copy was opened (our file times only; an 800-pixel copy of B.146 p.54 and Brymner's 1887 calendar OCR were already on disk from earlier work, not in the freezing agent's declared inputs).

Held-out test against the 25 Sep clear copies, as scored on 12 Nov: 56 of 58 unqualified word predictions agree (failures 43-19, 9-8). That scorer filled in the clear word from the prediction where it had no hand alignment; the 13 Nov re-score below supersedes it.
25 Sep aligned in full after the test; 39 new code associations recorded as post-clear and untested.

Brymner's calendars (Report on Canadian Archives 1885 and 1887, OCR) checked: summaries of all three letters, no full text and no cipher; catalogue.json, leads.json, targets, issues and pull requests searched: no overlap beyond Brice Dudout's 1779 pointer (#359) on lead 1137.

A second AI agent of ours, not shown our conclusions, reran the predictions byte for byte, rechecked 26 groups on the images (24 confirmed, 2 wrong: Clinton 43-19 is thousand on p.8; 25 Sep unit 129 has seven pairs, escaped) and found that the 12 Nov scorer defaulted clear words to the predictions.

Every unit of the 25 Sep letter hand-aligned with B.148 p.102 independently of the predictions (posttest/clear_alignment_25sep.tsv) and re-scored: 55 of 58 unqualified word predictions agree; failures 22-19 thence (clear there, both copies), 43-19 hundred (thousand), 9-8 has (have). Qualified 21 of 25, spelled 36 of 43 as frozen. Shuffled-table control, 200 shuffles: mean 0.44, max 15, none reaches 55.

Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections vols. 9-11 and 19-20 (Internet Archive OCR): Clinton 22 Feb 1782 printed in full in vol. 20 pp. 2-4; Carleton 6 and 25 Sep not found. HMC Report on American Manuscripts in the Royal Institution vol. III (1907): both Carleton letters calendared as headings with locations, no text.

Strict measure (measure_strict.py): 510 of 559 cipher units give the clear-copy word unchanged from the key and table (Clinton 0.881, 6 Sep 0.945, 25 Sep 0.940); spelled mismatches, the unread unit, glare and conflicting codes not counted. (recomputed after the 13 Nov corrections)

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1088 tokens, 406 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.031 per letter; random keys -3.151 (z 13.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.148 (mean -2.174, z 8.6); annealer on the real text -2.08. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.03; polyphony 0.017; 89 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.08

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The word-code table was rebuilt by aligning the ciphers with clear copies kept in the same archive, and the spelling key is Haldimand's Army List page; the table frozen from the February letter then predicted the September letter before its clear copy was opened (55 of 58).

texts.summary: Chief Justice Smith's intelligence of an American plan to invade Canada, Lafayette gone to France to propose it; George Rogers Clark to move down the Ohio and up the Wabash against Detroit; Congress said to have agreed to give Canada to France.
texts.note: read_share is 1 - hole rate on research/reading_audit/v2_score.py. The strict share of cipher units that the key and table give unchanged is 0.881 (measure_strict.py). 43-19 corrected to thousand after the test (posttest/corrections.tsv).

texts.summary: Carleton approves Haldimand's dealings with the Vermonters, regrets the Indian raids, will not come to Quebec; part of Pigot's fleet arrived.
texts.note: Every unit aligns with the clear register copy; one spelled word gives dit for did. Strict share 0.945 because four occurrences of codes with conflicting readings across the letters (11-1, 5-22) are not counted.

texts.summary: Two expeditions into the Indian country, Potter from Fort Muncy towards the Seneca country and Irwin from Fort Pitt towards Lake Erie; Paterson in Nova Scotia ordered to assist; Washington at Verplanck's Point; L'Aigle taken in the Delaware.
texts.note: read_share is 1 - hole rate on research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; the five codes whose frozen value disagrees with the clear copy (22-19, 13-14, 5-22, 9-8, 11-1) are holes. Aligned with the 13 Nov hand alignment and the escaped correction. Strict share 0.940.

The held-out test is the core result: 55 of 58 unqualified word predictions on a letter whose clear copy was opened only after the freeze, by our own agents' file times; a shuffled table averages 0.44. Prior readings exist in the archive (the clear copies) and Clinton's letter is printed in full (MPHC vol. 20, 1892), so this is not a first reading of the messages.
